name: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
description: Reverse-engineering tools for agents, served over MCP: inspect websites, JavaScript/Electron apps, .NET assemblies, APKs, packages, firmware, and (with Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA) native binaries, with the evidence behind every finding.

install.setup: npm install --global rea-agents, then register it with your agents (nexus-integrations.js rea register) and copy its skill into Nexus (nexus-integrations.js rea sync-skill).

invocation.summary: Each coding agent starts `rea mcp` itself and calls REA's tools directly, guided by the reverse-engineer-anything skill. Nexus only checks readiness, prints the registration commands, and keeps that skill in step with the installed CLI.

io.input: A local target the user supplies (app bundle, binary, ASAR or JavaScript tree, APK, .NET assembly, firmware, saved network capture) or a website URL, plus a question about how something works
io.output: Findings with their evidence (code, references, observations, and what stays unknown) returned to the agent; optional Evidence JSON files

limitations: Native binary analysis needs Hopper, Ghidra 12.1.x, or IDA, which Nexus does not install. Websites, JavaScript/Electron, .NET, APK and package inspection work without one.
Registering REA edits each agent's own config file (for example ~/.claude.json), so Nexus prints the command and the user runs it.
Runtime capture (browser, Electron, process, device) runs or drives the target under the user's account; static inspection only reads files.
Some targets are Linux-only: firmware extraction, packet and logic-signal recordings, ELF diagnostics, recorded crashes.
Use findings to understand behaviour and write your own implementation; check the target's licence or terms before analysing commercial software, and don't copy recovered code.
